If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, adjust forecast mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect momentum reversal, adding 1–2% to forecast if sentiment >0.67, or subtracting 1–2% if sentiment <0.33.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price has been trending upward, reduce forecast late horizon (16–30 days) by 0.5–1.5% to account for potential exhaustion.

If sentiment is neutral and price has been trending downward, increase forecast late horizon (16–30 days) by 0.5–1.5% to counteract downward momentum.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.00–1.00) and forecast deviates >1.5% from true path, apply a 1–2% correction in mid-horizon (8–15 days) toward the sentiment-weighted mean of recent 5-day sentiment.
